Grace / team — answers below for the SCIM/admin role sections. I pasted the key bits for the spreadsheet and attached a quick diagram to the shared Drive link.

- SCIM: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning. We handle incremental delta syncs and full syncs. Attribute mapping: we provide a UI for default mappings and an override layer at the tenant scope; per-tenant overrides are stored as tenant config and applied during provisioning. We support custom attribute passthrough and can map external group IDs to internal roles.

- Soft-delete / recovery: deleted users can be soft-deleted for a configurable retention window (default 30 days) before permanent purge; during soft-delete they remain in archive and still appear in audit exports.

- Admin delegation & elevation: we have a Role-Based Access Control model with built-in roles (Account Admin, Tenant Admin, Read-Only Auditor) and support custom roles. Time-limited elevation is available via Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation tokens tied to SSO sessions; durations are configurable and recorded in audit logs. Elevation requests can be approved by a designated approver group and are visible in the audit trail.

- Multi-tenant scoping: tenant admins have scoping boundaries; role assignments include a tenant_id and optional object-scoped permissions (e.g., dataset-level).

- Audit mapping: every UI action that changes configuration or data emits an event with: actor_id, actor_email, action_type, target_id, timestamp, request_id, source_ip. We expose read-only CSV/JSON exports and a streaming webhook for SIEM ingestion. Retention policy is configurable up to 7 years for enterprise customers.

I'll drop sample CSV audit export and a short how-to snippet into the Drive folder tonight.

Karthik
Engineering Manager, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: StellarRow RFI — audit export samples and retention

Grace — attached is a sanitized sample of our admin audit export (CSV) and a short note on redaction and retention. Highlights:

- Export columns included: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, action_type, object_type, object_id, prior_value_summary, new_value_summary, request_id, source_ip
- Redaction: we redact PII fields in exports by default; customers may opt-in to include certain fields for auditor use under an approved Data Use Agreement.
- Retention: default 1 year; enterprise plans may configure up to 7 years. We support HSM-backed retention locks for regulatory cases.

I'll add the CSV and a short retention-policy PDF to the Drive link.

Marissa
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Grace — thanks for the thorough packet; we reviewed the spreadsheet and the diagrams. A couple of quick clarifications before Security schedules the call: 

1) For time-limited elevation: can the approver be external to Redwood (i.e., StellarRow's own approval system via SAML assertion) or must approvals use Redwood's internal approver groups? If external approver is possible, what assertion format do you accept?
2) For audit exports: we need to be sure the exported event includes the original SSO Subject NameID when actions are performed via federated SSO — can you confirm the log schema includes Subject NameID or an equivalent stable subject claim?

If you can answer those two items today, Security will triage and then we can lock a 30-minute slot for Wed 29 Sep 10am PT.

Best,
Alex Barton
